messages:
sasha: CI canary push failing on registry after the Dockerfile tweak. build #8932 -> push dies mid-upload with 'unexpected EOF while reading response'. Anyone seen this with symlink layers?

ci-bot: Build 8932 failed during push to registry.redwood-internal.io/redwood/canary:sha-7b2f
Logs snippet:
```
failed to upload blob chunk: unexpected EOF
PUT /v2/redwood/canary/blobs/uploads/1234 HTTP/1.1" 502 256 "-"
error: upload aborted
```

miguel: can you paste the dockerfile diff + the exact build/push command? Also which uploader (kaniko/buildkit/docker)?

sasha: we switched to kaniko in the canary runner last week. Dockerfile diff: 
```
- COPY helpers/ /app/helpers/
+ ADD helpers/ /app/helpers/
+ RUN ln -s /app/helpers/bin/entrypoint /entrypoint-link
```
Build command in CI: `kaniko --context $CI_CONTEXT --destination registry.redwood-internal.io/redwood/canary:sha-7b2f`

jen: hmm ADD vs COPY shouldn't matter usually, but symlink creation might be odd for the tar layer. Kaniko does parallel chunk uploads; try lowering concurrency or single upload: `--max-concurrent-uploads=1` and rerun the job. Also try disabling compression to see layer size behavior.

ina: small note — we've seen registry proxy (bastion) reset connections when a single chunk stream is unusually long (symlinked files that resolve outside context can blow up the tar stream). could be S3 backend returning ECONNRESET.

sasha: reran with `--max-concurrent-uploads=1` and `--snapshotMode=redo` — progressed past previous EOF, then hit `413 Request Entity Too Large` on a different blob id. logs: 
```
PUT /v2/.../blobs/uploads/abcd HTTP/1.1" 413 0 "-"
response: request entity too large
```

miguel: can you try reproducing locally with kaniko (same version) and the exact context tar? If local reproduces we can bisect the dockerfile change. If local doesn't, this smells like registry/proxy flake. Please file a rerun request for older commit that used COPY (pre-change).

sasha: queued a CI rerun for commit 17a3c2 (pre-symlink). That one passed push OK. so failure correlates to the symlink layer. Starting a bisect: 17a3c2 -> current.

registry-bot: noticed high worker mem on upload-worker-12 at 2026-03-12T14:22:11Z, restarted container. logs: `read ECONNRESET from s3, streaming abort` — repeating pattern for large multipart PUTs.

miguel: ok that aligns. Two-pronged: (1) infra: investigate proxy/worker mem pressure and S3 errors (ping @eng-infra on the incident channel), (2) dev: avoid creating symlinked files that affect tar headers, or make kaniko use `--tar-include-file` workaround.

sasha: filing infra ticket with the worker logs and kaniko trace. I'll also update the Dockerfile back to using COPY+post-build symlink creation in CI container to avoid changing archive layout.

jen: thanks. could you add a short note in the repo runbook about `kaniko --max-concurrent-uploads=1` as a workaround? saved us time. :thumbsup:

sasha: will do and link the rerun/bisect PR. cc'ing @miguel and @ina for follow-ups. (reaction :eyes:)
